issues.body: The literal envelope defines graph_id as an absolute IRI or zero length for the default graph, while RDF 1.1 datasets can use a blank node as a graph name. The later skolemization requirement covers only protected triple subjects, not graph names. A conforming client therefore has no specified behavior for a valid named graph with a blank-node name: using its serialization-local blank-node label makes AAD unstable across round trips, while independently skolemizing it can produce incompatible AAD and undecryptable literals.
issues.fix_hint: Either restrict Profile SE explicitly to datasets whose named-graph names are IRIs and require refusal before sealing otherwise, or require blank-node graph names to be skolemized to stable absolute IRIs before sealing under a specified ownership/stability rule. Add a cross-implementation vector or refusal test for a blank-node graph name.
issues.title: Literal AAD does not define valid blank-node graph names

verdict.summary: Round 3 fixes both round-2 blockers: RDF identifiers now have one exact-code-point UTF-8 encoding with explicit absolute-IRI, length, and default-graph rules, and equality-tag inputs no longer normalize lexical forms or datatype IRIs. One completeness/interoperability defect remains: RDF 1.1 datasets permit blank nodes as graph names, but the literal envelope only defines graph_id for an absolute IRI or the default graph and gives no rejection or skolemization rule for a blank-node graph name. Different clients may improvise unstable blank-node labels or incompatible skolemization, making protected literals fail authentication after interchange. Because this is a newly identified major finding, progress is regressing under the required comparison scale, despite the prior findings being repaired.
